facts.statement: Antetonitrus lived during the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Jurassic,

facts.statement: The animal belongs to the genus Antetonitrus.
facts.quote: genus: Antetonitrus

facts.statement: The only known species is Antetonitrus ingenipes.
facts.quote: species: ingenipes

facts.statement: The genus was named by Yates and Kitching in 2003.
facts.quote: authority: Yates & Kitching, 2003

facts.statement: Antetonitrus is a sauropodiform dinosaur found in the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation of South Africa.
facts.quote: Antetonitrus is a genus of sauropodiform dinosaur found in the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation of South Africa.

facts.statement: Antetonitrus was a quadrupedal herbivore that used its forelimbs for grasping rather than just for weight support.
facts.quote: It was a quadrupedal herbivore, like its later relatives, but shows primitive adaptations to use the forelimbs for grasping, instead of purely for weight support.

facts.statement: Adam Yates and James Kitching named Antetonitrus in a 2003 report.
facts.quote: Adam Yates, an Australian expert on early sauropodomorphs, named Antetonitrus in a 2003 report co-authored by South African James Kitching.

facts.statement: The species name ingenipes means "massive foot" because it shows early development of feet designed for weight support.
facts.quote: The one known species of Antetonitrus is called A. ingenipes, from the Latin ingens ("massive") and pes ("foot"), because it shows the beginning of the development of feet designed solely to support weight.

facts.statement: Kitching discovered the fossils in 1981 in the Free State of South Africa, where they were initially labeled as Euskelosaurus.
facts.quote: The fossils now known as Antetonitrus were discovered by Kitching in 1981 in the Free State of South Africa, and were stored in the Bernard Price Institute where they were labeled as Euskelosaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of vertebrae and numerous bones from the forelimbs and hind limbs, presumed to be from one individual.
facts.quote: The holotype, or original specimen, consists of several vertebrae and numerous bones from both forelimb and hind limb, all presumed to be from one individual.

facts.statement: Five additional limb bones from a smaller individual were also assigned to the genus.
facts.quote: Five more limb bones from another smaller individual were also referred to the genus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen may have measured 8 to 10 meters in length, 1.5 to 2 meters in hip height, and 5.6 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen may have measured 8 - 10 m in length, 1.5 - 2 m in hip height and 5.6 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The unfused neural arches suggest the holotype individual may not have been fully grown.
facts.quote: However, the neural arches of the vertebrae were not fused with the centra, indicating that this individual perhaps was not fully grown.

facts.statement: Unlike its smaller ancestors, Antetonitrus was primarily quadrupedal.
facts.quote: Unlike most of its smaller and more lightly built ancestors, Antetonitrus was primarily quadrupedal.

facts.statement: The first digit of the hand was twisted and flexible, capable of grasping.
facts.quote: However, the first digit of the hand, also called the "thumb" or pollex, was still twisted and flexible, capable of grasping against the hand.

facts.statement: The femur was slightly S-curved in lateral view, unlike the straight femur of other sauropods.
facts.quote: The femur was slightly sigmoidal (S-curved) in lateral view rather than straight as in other sauropods.

facts.statement: Yates and Kitching classified Antetonitrus as a basal sauropod between more derived animals like Isanosaurus and more basal sauropods like Melanorosaurus.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis by Yates and Kitching recognizes Antetonitrus as a basal sauropod, occupying a position between more derived animals such as Isanosaurus or Vulcanodon, and more basal sauropods like Melanorosaurus.

facts.statement: Apaldetti et al. (2018) established the clade Lessemsauridae to include Antetonitrus, Lessemsaurus, and Ingentia.
facts.quote: Apaldetti et al. (2018) erected Lessemsauridae, a clade containing Antetonitrus, Lessemsaurus and Ingentia.

facts.statement: The parent group of Antetonitrus is Lessemsauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lessemsauridae

facts.statement: Antetonitrus belongs to the family Lessemsauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Lessemsauridae

facts.statement: Antetonitrus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Antetonitrus lived from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian stages, between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Antetonitrus is one of the oldest known sauropods chronologically, tied with others from the same formation.
facts.quote: While Antetonitrus is not the earliest sauropod from a phylogenetic standpoint, it is currently one of the oldest known sauropod chronologically, or rather tied for that distinction with other early sauropods from the same formation, like Melanorosaurus and Blikanasaurus.

facts.statement: Studies indicate Antetonitrus was recovered from the Early Jurassic Upper Elliot Formation.
facts.quote: Later studies indicate that it was actually recovered from the Early Jurassic Upper Elliot Formation.

facts.statement: Before Antetonitrus was recognized as a sauropod, Isanosaurus from Thailand was considered the oldest known sauropod.
facts.quote: Before Antetonitrus and the other animals recovered from the Elliot Formation were recognized as sauropods, the oldest known sauropod had been Isanosaurus from the Rhaetian stage of Thailand.

facts.statement: Early sauropods and relatives were found worldwide because continents were united as Pangaea.
facts.quote: Early sauropods and their sauropodomorph relatives were found around the world as all of the continents were at the time united into the single supercontinent, Pangaea, which made dispersal across the entire terrestrial world possible.

rejected.statement: The name Antetonitrus means "before thunder" and refers to its existence before other known sauropods like Brontosaurus.
rejected.quote: The name is derived from the Latin ante- ("before") and tonitrus ("thunder"), which refers to its existence, before other known sauropods, specifically Brontosaurus ("thunder lizard").

rejected.statement: Antetonitrus had forelimbs much longer relative to its hind legs than earlier animals, and a shortened metatarsus.
rejected.quote: Like sauropods, its forelimbs were much longer relative to its hind legs than earlier animals, while the metatarsus was shortened.
